1.explanation: The only place in the repo that defines the syntax and escape-sequence handling for .properties files is src/languages/properties.js. It contains the rules for interpreting a trailing '\' as a line continuation and for recognizing escape sequences. Because the misbehavior occurs when the parser confuses an escaped backslash at end-of-line with a continuation marker, the fix must be made in the grammar definitions in this file.
1.bug_scenario: In a .properties file, values can span lines if the line ends with a single backslash (“\”). However, when the very last character of a value is itself an escaped backslash (i.e. “\\” in the source), the grammar in properties.js still treats that final backslash as a line-continuation marker. The result is that the trailing backslash is swallowed, the next line’s text is merged into the value, and both the value and following lines are mis-highlighted.

2.explanation: The only place where the Properties mode is defined is in `src/languages/properties.js`. That file contains the logic (regex and mode definitions) that recognize backslash escapes and line continuations. Because it does not properly distinguish a single backslash at end-of-line (true continuation) from an escaped backslash (`\\`), it always assumes continuation. Fixing this file so it only treats an unescaped backslash as a continuation marker will resolve the issue.
2.bug_scenario:
In the Properties highlighter, a backslash at end of a line is always treated as a line-continuation marker. When the intended value really ends in an escaped backslash (`\\`), the parser still thinks there’s a continuation and so it swallows the next line (merging the next property into the previous value). This shows up when highlighting something like:

a = a1\
    a2
b = b\\
c = c

Instead of treating `b = b\\` as a complete value of `b\\`, it treats the trailing `\\` as `\` + continuation and merges `c = c` into `b`’s value.
